hook_text: Why does milk go sour, meat go rotten and wounds get infected? A French scientist found the tiny culprits.
clip_script: France, the eighteen-sixties. Louis Pasteur peers into a microscope and sees tiny living things in spoiled wine. In his famous experiment, broth in a flask with a long, curved neck stays fresh, because germs from the air get trapped in the bend. Germs do not appear from nowhere. They come from the air, and they make things rot and people ill. Heating kills them: that is pasteurisation. His work also gave us vaccines against anthrax and rabies.
visual_style: Whiteboard microscope view of wriggling germs, then two flasks, one with a straight neck turning cloudy and one with a swan neck staying clear, then a milk carton labelled pasteurised.
mood: Curious and clever, like a science experiment that changes everything.
pacing: A puzzle first, then a clear step-by-step experiment, then the big results.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the word pasteurised on a product at home.
